title: Restricting a right-fraction localization to a subcategory with enough denominators
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and $W$ a class of its morphisms containing identities and closed under composition. Assume the right-fraction axioms: for $f:X\to Z$ and $s:Y\to Z$ with $s\in W$ there are $t:T\to X$ in $W$ and $g:T\to Y$ with $ft=sg$; and whenever $f,g:X\to Y$ and $s:Y\to Z$ in $W$ satisfy $sf=sg$, there is $t:T\to X$ in $W$ with $ft=gt$. In the first axiom only $s$, not $f$, is required to lie in $W$. Let $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal C$ be a full subcategory, and assume that every $X\in\mathcal C$ admits an arrow $s:B\to X$ in $W$ with $B\in\mathcal B$. Put $W_{\mathcal B}=W\cap\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal B)$. Then $W_{\mathcal B}$ has a right calculus of fractions, and the inclusion induces an equivalence $\mathcal B[W_{\mathcal B}^{-1}]\to\mathcal C[W^{-1}]$, where localization is in the universal-property sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Categories and localizations are taken in a common larger universe. Neither a functorial choice of the arrows $B\to X$ nor a triangulated structure is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GSL (lemma-localization-subcategory), proof by refining right-fraction sources into the full subcategory. This is the categorical right-calculus form of that proof: replace its triangulated and saturation hypotheses by the stated right-fraction axioms; it is not the verbatim triangulated statement.
